- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) or contains negative spikes, model often underestimates downside risk; add downward buffer or adjust mean reversion threshold.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply decay or smoothing to subsequent forecasts.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80–85), model often fails to correct; adjust forecast to align with recent mean or volatility-adjusted baseline.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average to dampen overconfidence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent trends; apply lagged smoothing or reduce forecast sensitivity to last 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to err on the side of conservatism; increase forecast range or allow for asymmetric volatility.
